exceptions.reason: The cases open a nested menu with a press and with the Enter key. The trigger of Menu in Vase UI has no press yet.

exceptions.title: moves focus to the next element when tabbing out of a nested menu inside the popover
exceptions.reason: The case presses the trigger of a nested menu to open it. The trigger of Menu in Vase UI has no press yet.

exceptions.title: keeps the popover open when Escape closes a nested dialog after a backdrop press
exceptions.reason: React sends the press of a portal up the React tree, so the popover counts a press on the backdrop of the nested dialog as inside. A Vue press goes up the DOM only. Vase UI counts a press in a child popup as inside through the capture listeners of the popup element of the child, and `Dialog.Backdrop` has no such listeners. The portal of the dialog puts the backdrop outside the popup of the popover, so a press on it closes the popover.

exceptions.title: hands off hover between detached triggers when the rendered component retains a stale ref
exceptions.reason: The case renders a component that keeps the first ref callback that it got. A part gives its ref callbacks one time, in `setup`, and the callback of a trigger only writes the element to a ref. A watcher on the element, the id and the store then registers the trigger on the store that it has at that time. A callback that a component keeps thus cannot register the trigger on the store that the trigger left.

exceptions.title: keeps registration on the attached store when a stale-ref component swaps its host node
exceptions.reason: The case renders a component that keeps the first ref callback that it got, and swaps its host node. A part gives its ref callbacks one time, in `setup`, and the callback of a trigger only writes the element to a ref. The watcher of the registration then moves the registration to the new element on the store that the trigger has at that time.

exceptions.title: does not detach the consumer ref when the handle attaches to a root
exceptions.reason: The case counts the calls of the ref callback of a consumer. React merges that callback with the ref callbacks of the part, and it makes a new merged ref when the store of the trigger changes. The consumer then gets a call with `null` and a new call. A part gives its own ref callbacks one time, in `setup`, so a change of the store changes none of them.
